fields.name: Requests
fields.evidence: esv::disarm::WeaponSystem::GenerateUnequipRequests (EoCServer.dll+0x37EF70) rebuilds the array from the frame data: AllocateInternal(n, 0x108, 8), copies qword +0, qword +8 and the rest with EoCServer.dll+0x37E650 (Script Extender UnequipRequest layout from +8). bg3.exe destructor bg3.exe+0x22AA0B0 -> bg3.exe+0x22E1950 destroys each 0x108-byte element at +0x28 (bg3.exe+0x21B8540). Element = {EntityHandle, SE inventory UnequipRequest (0x100)}; the optional/variant members are flattened. Live (seen.py, idle): one instance, all bytes zero (empty container).

open_questions: DropMovement.PathSettings (80 bytes, SE path::Settings with std::variant members) stays opaque bytes: it cannot be written with the build's primitive types; the element is {EntityHandle, SE esv inventory UnequipRequest (0x100)} and is better declared by hand with SE's own UnequipRequest than generated.

Offsets of the members from +0x08 to +0x47 and from +0xF0 on rest on the Toolkit (EoCServer.dll+0x37EF70 / +0x37E650) and SE's UnequipRequest; on Windows only the stride 0x108, Level/HasLevel at +0x48/+0x4C, DropMovement at +0x50 with flag +0xE8 and the STDString inside it are confirmed.
Meaning of the first EntityHandle (+0) of the element.
status_reason: only empty (all-zero) instances were seen: the member boundaries are untested
second_pass: Windows destructors bg3.exe+0x22E1950 -> bg3.exe+0x21B8540 -> bg3.exe+0x21BCD00 confirm the 0x108 stride, the optional Level (+0x48/+0x4C), the optional DropMovement (+0x50/+0xE8) and the STDString at DropMovement+0x80; the custom 24-byte string struct is replaced by STDString. Not settled for the build: the path settings stay opaque and the remaining members rest on the Toolkit.
